title: Cheap power decides who keeps mining
description:
Cheap power decides who keeps mining

In this short: what the mining data actually shows this week, and what it means for a miner.

• Flexible mining load is increasingly used as a demand-response asset, absorbing power during curtailment windows rather than competing for it at peak. (Pickaxe, 2026-11-04)
• Flared-gas and stranded-gas sites remain the cheapest power source for containerised mining, because the operator is paid to remove a waste stream. (bitcoin.com, 2026-11-06)
• Efficiency of the installed fleet is roughly 22 joules per terahash, which sets the floor on how cheap power must be to stay profitable at current hashprice. (Cointribune, 2026-11-22)
• At a hashprice of 26.16 USD per PH/s per day, a 22 J/TH machine needs power below roughly 0.05 USD per kWh to cover power cost alone. (Cointribune, 2026-11-22)
